package_info.package_name: Trojanized jQuery (multiple packages, e.g., icnes, stylesyosx, imagegs, etc.)
package_info.package_manager: npm (also distributed via GitHub and jsDelivr CDN)
package_info.package_versions: Multiple (see list, e.g., icnes@8.0.0, stylesyosx@9.0.3, etc.)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain a trojanized version of jQuery where the 'end' prototype function is modified to exfiltrate all form data from the page to attacker-controlled domains whenever it is called, either directly or indirectly (e.g., via fadeTo). The packages are distributed under misleading names, often include personal files, and use unique exfiltration URLs to evade detection.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (whenever jQuery's end or fadeTo is called in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: jquery.min.js, all-min.js, slim.js (and other variants in package root or distributed via CDN)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the end function is called (directly or via fadeTo), the code serializes all form data on the page, encodes it as a hex string, and sends it via a non-blocking GET request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled URL, enabling exfiltration of sensitive user input.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The end function is not expected to perform network requests or access form data; its legitimate purpose is to return the previous jQuery object in a chain.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal jQuery end returns the previous object for chaining; the malicious version exfiltrates form data to a remote server.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry might collect form data, but only with user consent and never in a core library function like end.
key_indicators: Network request in a core library prototype method
Exfiltration of all form data without user interaction

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when icons.js or min.js is loaded and executed in the browser)
execution_context.file_location: icons.js, min.js (in package root or distributed via CDN)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects external scripts into the page, including a deprecated version of Ionicons and a remote script (slim.js) hosted on jsDelivr, which itself contains the trojanized jQuery. This enables further malicious payload delivery and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Injecting remote scripts from untrusted sources is a common technique for loading additional malware. The use of outdated libraries and misleading warnings is intended to trick users.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal icon libraries do not inject unrelated remote scripts or force outdated versions without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic script injection is used in some legitimate plugin loaders, but not in core icon libraries and not with misleading warnings.
key_indicators: Injection of remote scripts from attacker-controlled CDN

attack_chain.action: User installs or includes a malicious package (npm, GitHub, or CDN).
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojanized jQuery or loader script is present in the application.

attack_chain.action: Malicious jQuery file (or loader script) is loaded and executed in the browser.
attack_chain.leads_to: Trojanized jQuery is present in the page context.

attack_chain.action: User or application code calls jQuery's end or fadeTo function (directly or indirectly).
All form data on the page is serialized, hex-encoded, and exfiltrated via GET request to attacker-controlled domain.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user input (credentials, PII, etc.).

behavioral_signatures: Modification of jQuery prototype methods (especially end) to include network requests
Unexpected network requests triggered by UI actions (e.g., fadeTo animation)
Hex-encoded form data sent to external domains
Dynamic injection of remote scripts from untrusted sources
file_indicators: jquery.min.js, all-min.js, slim.js, registration.min.js, icon.min.js, fontawesome.js (with modified end function)
Presence of personal files (npm cache, npm logs, termux.properties) in package root
network_indicators: Requests to jsdelivr.net/gh/indexsc/libs/slim.js or similar GitHub-backed CDN URLs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan JavaScript dependencies for modifications to core library prototype methods (especially jQuery's end). Monitor for unexpected network requests containing serialized or hex-encoded form data sent to suspicious domains. Flag packages that include personal files or inject remote scripts from untrusted sources. Use static analysis to compare jQuery source code against known-good versions and alert on any added network or data exfiltration logic.
